title: Refyard GitService contract
description: Generated from packages/git-contract by `pnpm check:contract`. Schemas are JSON-Schema exports of the Zod schemas; request validation is authoritative in the Zod source, and its semantic rules (branch-name grammar, URL schemes, path containment) are intentionally not expressible here.

AbortCherryPickOperation.description: Abort the cherry-pick in progress and restore the state it started from. When Git cannot restore it, the diagnostic is reported and nothing is reset.

AbortMergeOperation.description: Abort the in-progress merge. When Git cannot restore the previous state, the diagnostic is reported instead of a reset fallback.

AbortRebaseOperation.description: Abort the rebase in progress and restore the branch to where the rebase started. When Git cannot restore it, the diagnostic is reported and nothing is reset.

AcknowledgeUncertainOperationRequest.description: Lifts the write block an uncertain operation left behind, after the caller has re-read state and confirmed against a fresh snapshot. It never rewrites the uncertain operation's outcome.

AddRemoteOperation.description: Add a remote, optionally with a separate push URL.

AddSubmoduleOperation.description: Add a submodule from an approved remote or local path. Arbitrary transport helpers are refused, and the destination is shown before any network connection.

AllowedRootId.description: A directory the service was explicitly granted, resolved by the host.

AmendCommitOperation.description: Rewrite the tip commit. `null` keeps the existing message. The UI must say a rewrite happened; this version performs no follow-up force push.

ApiMajor.description: Public API major version. A mismatch means the client must not call write endpoints.

ApplyStashOperation.description: Apply a stash and keep it. The locator must still resolve to the given object.

BranchName.description: A short branch name such as `main` or `feature/graph-paging`.

CancelOperationRequest.description: Cancel an operation that has not started. A running mutation is not cancellable in this version.

CapabilitiesQuery.description: Which target the answer should describe. Empty keeps the original meaning: the host's default local target. Naming both a target and a repository that do not belong together is InvalidRequest — never a silent fallback to local.

CapabilitiesResponse.description: What this build can do right now. An operation missing from `operations` is not implemented or not safe on this machine; it is never reported as available and then refused.

CherryPickOperation.description: Apply one commit's change onto the checked-out branch as a new commit, keeping the original message and author. A merge commit is refused: picking which parent to keep is a decision this build does not make. A conflict stops the operation into the same resolve-and-continue state a merge uses.

ClientRequestId.description: Client-chosen idempotency key. Reusing it with a different payload is a conflict, not a retry.

CloneRepositoryOperation.description: Clone an approved remote into an approved root. Submodules are initialised only when asked; credential helpers are the target machine’s.

CommitDetail.description: Full commit metadata and message, decoded through the host text codec.

CommitMessage.description: Message passed on stdin as UTF-8 bytes. Maximum 1048576 bytes; empty or whitespace-only messages are rejected.

CommitOperation.description: Commit the current index with the given message. Nothing is staged implicitly, no empty commit is created, and user hooks and signing settings stay in force.

CommitSummary.description: One row of history. `boundary` marks a shallow/grafted edge and `missingParents` names parents whose objects are absent, so a UI never draws an unloaded parent as a root.

ContinueCherryPickOperation.description: Commit the resolved index of a cherry-pick that stopped for conflicts, using the original message. Refused while any conflicted path is still unmerged.

ContinueMergeOperation.description: Complete a merge after the conflicted paths were resolved outside and staged.

ContinueRebaseOperation.description: Resume the rebase in progress after its stopped commit was resolved and staged. Refused while any conflicted path is still unmerged.

CreateBranchOperation.description: Create a branch, optionally at a specific commit and optionally checked out.

CreateStashOperation.description: Stash working-tree changes. Ignored files are never included, and submodules are not stashed recursively.

CreateTagOperation.description: Create a lightweight tag (`annotation: null`) or an annotated one. An existing tag is never overwritten.

CreateTargetRequest.description: Selects where future Git work runs: this machine, a candidate from the host list, or a manually entered alias bound to the config source it should be read from. Credentials are never part of this request.

CreateWorktreeOperation.description: Add a linked worktree inside an approved root. A branch already checked out elsewhere stays refused.

Cursor.description: Opaque continuation for a paged read; never parsed by clients.

DeleteBranchOperation.description: Delete a fully merged local branch. Unmerged branches are refused; there is no force delete.

DeleteTagOperation.description: Delete one local tag. Remote tags are never touched.

DiffFile.description: One changed file with its bounded patch.

DiffQuery.description: A diff is always bounded and always scoped: worktree-vs-index, index-vs-HEAD, one commit, or a two-point range. `pathId` restricts it to one path.

DiffResponse.description: A bounded diff read: selected paths, one commit, or a two-point range.

DiscardTrackedPathsOperation.description: Restore selected tracked files from the index — not from HEAD — after backing up what the change would destroy. Untracked, ignored, symlink and submodule paths are refused.

DisconnectTargetRequest.description: Releases one target this session owns. It must not tear down connections another session is still using.

DisplayPath.description: Escaped, human-readable form of a path. For display only: never send it back as an operation input.

DropCommitOperation.description: Remove one commit from the checked-out branch by replaying its descendants onto its parent. A merge commit and the branch's first commit are refused, and the commit must be on the checked-out branch. A conflict during the replay stops into the same resolve-and-continue state a merge uses; a descendant that becomes empty is dropped with the target.

DropStashOperation.description: Discard one stash entry. This is a repository-level change; it cannot be undone from the UI.

EventEnvelope.description: One event with its monotonic sequence number, so a client can detect a gap and re-read.

EventPayload.description: SSE payload. Events are hints that invalidate cached reads; they are never the only source of truth.

EventsQuery.description: Event stream. `since` resumes after a sequence number; if the ring no longer holds that point, the stream starts with an `eventGap`.

ExecutionTargetKind.description: Where Git runs: this machine, or a specific host the user selected from their SSH configuration.

ExecutionTargetState.description: Connection state of one execution target. Only `ready` may be read from; `unavailable` carries a problem, never an empty result.

ExecutionTargetSummary.description: One target a session can run Git against. `generation` changes when the target is rebuilt — a re-read of configuration, a reconnect — and invalidates snapshots, cursors and previews bound to the previous one.

FetchOperation.description: Fetch one remote. Each ref’s outcome is reported separately; the result is a change to remote-tracking refs, never to local branches.

FilePatch.description: Text patches are bounded and parsed; a synthesized patch means the file is untracked and its content came from an authorised read, not from Git.

FilesystemEntriesQuery.description: A person-entered local path to browse. The host expands a leading ~/ against its own home directory and returns directories only.

FilesystemEntriesResponse.description: Bounded directory entries for the explicit local repository picker; file contents are never returned.

FilesystemEntry.description: One directory the authenticated local path selector may navigate to or open.

FullRefName.description: Fully qualified ref such as `refs/heads/main` or `refs/tags/v1.0.0`. Explicit source and destination refs keep a push from inheriting surprise refspecs.

GitCapabilities.description: Machine formats probed on this machine, not inferred from a version string. A missing format removes the dependent feature from `operations`.

HeadState.description: `unborn` is a repository with no commits yet — not an error, and not a missing branch.

HealthResponse.description: Liveness only. A 200 here does not prove the listener is this service, so the CLI verifies identity out of band before opening a browser.

HistoryPage.description: A page of the commit graph in topological order. Paging continues from a cursor bound to the tips it started with; `tipsMoved` tells the UI the branch advanced, and the old page is still served from the old tips rather than re-interpreted.

HistoryQuery.description: History page request. `cursor` continues a page from the tips it started with; `detailOid` additionally returns one full commit message.

HostCapabilities.description: Host-level abilities. `localFolderPicker` is true only where the host can open a real OS directory dialog; a browser must use the path picker instead.

HostKind.description: The runtime answering this API. `rust` is the native host; `node` is the packaged service. Neither implies the other's capabilities.

HostWarning.description: Something the host could not fully account for while answering — for example a conditional Include it will not evaluate. Warnings accompany partial answers; they are not errors.

InitRepositoryOperation.description: Create a repository at the workspace destination. `null` uses Git’s default branch name.

LockWorktreeOperation.description: Lock a linked worktree, with an optional reason.

MergeOperation.description: Merge one explicit commit into the current branch. Conflicts stop the operation with unmerged index stages shown; they are never auto-resolved.

MutationRequest.description: A closed mutation: idempotency key, the resource it addresses, and the operation. Unknown keys and unknown operation kinds are rejected.

MutationTarget.description: Discriminated by `kind`; an operation accepts only the kinds it declares.

ObjectFormat.description: Hash format of a repository, as reported by Git, never assumed.

ObjectId.description: Git object name. The accepted lengths are the known object formats; the repository decides which one applies.

OperationAccepted.description: The operation was recorded durably. It has not run yet, and may still fail.

OperationId.description: A submitted mutation. Also the handle for querying its outcome.

OperationRecord.description: A journal entry as the client sees it. The journal itself stores metadata and payload digests, never diffs, messages, tokens or credentials.

OperationResult.description: What a finished operation reports: re-read facts and the invalidation the UI must act on, not Git’s stdout text.

OperationStatus.description: Terminal states are `succeeded`, `failed`, `needsAttention`, `unknown` and `cancelled`. `unknown` means Git may have changed things and the service will not guess or retry.

OperationsListQuery.description: Recent operations for the requesting actor; with `operationId` a single record, which is how a client checks an operation after losing the response.

OperationsListResponse.description: Recent operations for the requesting actor.

PatchHunk.description: A parsed hunk, so the UI renders lines without re-parsing patch grammar.

PatchLine.description: One patch line without its leading marker; `noNewline` carries the end-of-file marker.

PathEncoding.description: Whether this path can be handed back for execution. `unrepresentable` paths are readable metadata only; operations mentioning them are rejected.

PathId.description: One path inside a worktree, bound to the raw bytes of that path. The only input accepted by path mutations.

PathSelection.description: Paths plus their content-fingerprint tokens; lengths must match exactly.

PlainPathSelection.description: Paths addressed by id, in this worktree.

PopStashOperation.description: Apply a stash and drop it on success only. A conflict leaves the stash in place for a human to resolve.

PreviewToken.description: Authorises acting on one path whose content fingerprint matched when the preview was taken.

PreviewsRequest.description: Ask for content fingerprints of selected paths before a stage or discard.

PreviewsResponse.description: Content fingerprints bound to paths. The tokens expire, and a token whose file changed is stale rather than silently still valid.

Problem.description: One failure, with enough detail for a UI decision.

ProblemCode.description: Closed set of failure codes. Clients branch on these, not on message text.

ProblemResponse.description: The body of any 4xx/5xx JSON response.

PullOperation.description: Fast-forward the current branch from its remote. A divergence fails: this version never merges or rebases implicitly, and it separates "remote-tracking refs updated" from "working branch not moved".

PushOperation.description: Push exactly one explicit source ref to one explicit destination ref. No mirroring, no implicit follow-tags, no force.

PushTagOperation.description: Push one tag by name, without force and without deleting anything remotely.

RebaseOperation.description: Replay the checked-out branch's own commits onto another commit. A conflict stops the operation into the same resolve-and-continue state a merge uses; finishing a replayed commit keeps its original message, and no editor is ever opened.

RefEntry.description: A local branch, with its upstream state when one is configured.

RefsSnapshot.description: Branches, remote-tracking refs, tags and remotes in one read. URLs are redacted for display; the host never returns a credential.

RegisterRepositoryRequest.description: The exact absolute path or ~/ shorthand a person selected for runtime approval. The host checks repository-ness and containment; it never scans for candidates.

RelativeDestination.description: Path relative to an approved root. Absolute paths, `..` segments and `.git` components are rejected by validation.

RemoteName.description: A configured remote name such as `origin`.

RemoteRefEntry.description: A remote-tracking ref, as observed locally after the last fetch.

RemoteUrl.description: https:// or ssh:// URL, scp-like `user@host:path`, or an absolute local path the user approved. Credentials are redacted before display or logging.

RemoveRemoteOperation.description: Remove a remote and its remote-tracking refs. Local branches are untouched.

RemoveWorktreeOperation.description: Remove a clean, non-primary, unlocked worktree. Git’s own refusal is reported as-is; nothing falls back to recursive deletion.

RepositoriesResponse.description: Registered repositories and the roots they were approved under. Registration is explicit; nothing is discovered by scanning the disk.

RepositoryId.description: One common Git directory. Worktrees share it; a second clone of the same project does not.

RepositoryQuery.description: Queries that address a repository — its refs, remotes, tags, worktree list.

RepositorySummary.description: One registered repository, as shown in the repository list.

RepositoryTarget.description: A repository-level change: refs, remotes, tags, worktrees, submodule wiring.

ResetBranchOperation.description: Move the checked-out branch to another commit. Soft keeps the index exactly as it is; mixed resets the index to the target commit, which unstages anything staged. The working tree is never touched and no content is lost: a mode that would discard it (Git's hard reset) is deliberately not offered. A merge or revert in progress is refused.

RevertCommitOperation.description: Create a commit that undoes one completed commit, with Git's own revert message and with the user's hooks running. A merge commit is refused: picking which parent to keep is a decision this build does not make. A conflict is aborted before it is reported, so the operation either completes or leaves nothing behind.

RevokeRepositoryRequest.description: Revokes one registered repository. The access audit is written before the live registry entry disappears.

RuntimeLimits.description: Limits the service enforces on reads, requests, queues and event streams.

ServiceInstanceId.description: Identifies one running service process; changes across restarts.

SessionExchangeRequest.description: Body of POST /api/v1/session/exchange. The ticket is single-use, short-lived and bound to one instance, origin, actor and resource set; an explicitly configured hosted origin also requires a password.

SessionExchangeResponse.description: An in-memory bearer session. Never persisted client-side.

SessionGrants.description: What this session is allowed to reach.

SetBranchUpstreamOperation.description: Set or clear (with `null`) the upstream of a local branch.

SnapshotId.description: A recorded read of mutable state. Mutations carry the snapshot they were planned against.

SshHostCandidate.description: One concrete alias read from an SSH config source. It is a candidate, not a verified machine: nothing here proves the host exists, is reachable, or has the key the user thinks it has.

SshHostId.description: A host candidate the service read from an SSH configuration source. An identifier, never a credential.

SshHostList.description: Host aliases read from configuration files, with the revision of the source set they came from. Reading this never contacts a server and never executes configuration.

SshSourceId.description: One SSH configuration source and its revision. Selecting a source is a trusted-host setting, so it is never supplied by a remote page as a free filesystem path.

StagePathsOperation.description: Stage exactly the selected paths. Renames include whichever old and new paths are required; nothing is staged recursively.

StashEntry.description: A stash entry. The locator is where it currently sits in the reflog and moves as stashes are added or dropped, so writes always carry the OID too.

StashLocator.description: Reflog locator of a stash entry, e.g. `stash@{2}`.

StashRef.description: A stash identified by object name, with the locator it was listed under. The host re-checks that the locator still points at that object before any write.

StatusEntry.description: One changed path. Status characters are Git’s own (`.`, `M`, `A`, `D`, `R`, `U`, …); the UI decides presentation, never re-parses them into meaning.

StatusSnapshot.description: Working-tree and index state at a point in time. `ahead`/`behind` describe local remote-tracking refs only — they are not the server’s state.

SubmoduleStatus.description: Submodule flags from porcelain v2’s `sub` field.

SubmoduleSummary.description: Three object names, never one "up to date" flag: what the parent commit records, what the parent index has, and what the submodule actually checked out.

SubmodulesResponse.description: Submodule state as seen from one worktree.

SwitchBranchOperation.description: Check out an existing branch. Never forced: a conflict with local changes is reported, not resolved by discarding them.

SyncSubmoduleOperation.description: Copy submodule URLs from the parent repository configuration into the submodules.

TagEntry.description: A tag. For an annotated tag `oid` is the tag object and `targetOid` the commit it points at.

TagName.description: A short tag name such as `v1.2.0`.

TargetGeneration.description: Opaque revision of a target's construction. Not an identity proof of the remote host; trust stays with OpenSSH's known_hosts policy.

TargetId.description: One execution target: where Git runs for this session. Minted by the host; the browser only names it back.

TargetKind.description: Which kind of resource a mutation addresses.

UnavailableReason.description: Why some operations are absent from this build.

UnlockWorktreeOperation.description: Unlock a worktree that was locked.

UnmergedStage.description: One index stage of a conflicted path: base, ours, theirs.

UnstagePathsOperation.description: Reset the selected paths in the index only. Working-tree files are never touched.

UpdateRemoteOperation.description: Rename a remote and/or change its URLs. At least one change must be present; null fields are left unchanged.

UpdateSubmoduleOperation.description: Check out the commit the parent repository records. `--remote` and `--force` are not available, and configured update shell commands are ignored.

WorkspaceTarget.description: A location inside an approved root, for operations that create repositories.

WorktreeId.description: One worktree of a repository, with its own HEAD and index.

WorktreeQuery.description: Queries that address a worktree. Omitting `worktreeId` selects the primary worktree.

WorktreeReference.description: What the new worktree checks out. A branch already checked out elsewhere is refused by Git, not overridden.

WorktreeSummary.description: Worktrees of one repository share its refs but have independent HEAD, index and files.

WorktreeTarget.description: A worktree-level change: index, working files, HEAD, merges, stashes.

WorktreesResponse.description: All worktrees of a repository, including the primary one.

__schema157.description: Only required for an explicitly configured hosted origin; never persisted or reused after this exchange.

__schema337.description: Trimmed single-line literal message search, 1–512 Unicode scalar values; semantic validation rejects NUL, CR/LF and unpaired surrogates.

__schema339.description: Trimmed single-line literal author search, 1–512 Unicode scalar values.
